prompt:
I need the front end for Plotyard. A course workspace for university data-visualization classes that holds the readings, datasets, student chart drafts and peer critique rounds for a whole term.

Who's using it: Dana Okafor, a second-year cognitive science undergraduate in a 140-student intro visualization course. She's comfortable with spreadsheets but new to the course's structure, and she missed week 5 because she was sick.

What they're doing right now: It's Tuesday of week 6. Problem Set 4 is due Thursday, and her peer critique of two classmates' drafts is due tonight. She just opened the PS4 brief, which points to a dataset and a reading from week 5 she never saw. She needs to work out where week 5's material lives, get to the right version of the dataset, then find the two drafts she's assigned to critique, and get back to her own PS4 draft without losing track of where she was.

What's in the system at this point: Course 'Visual Explanation of Data', Fall 2026, 10 weeks in 4 modules (Perception, Encoding, Interaction, Narrative). 23 readings, 14 datasets (e.g., 'San Diego bike counts 2019–2025, 6 versions; PS4 uses v3', 'Global coffee exports by country, 1990–2024', 'Campus dining waste, daily kg'). 5 problem sets with briefs, rubrics and due dates; PS4 'Encoding comparisons' due Thu Nov 19 11:59pm. Dana's PS4 draft has 3 chart attempts and was last saved 2 days ago. Critique Round 3: she's assigned draft #A-0817 by 'Student 31' and draft #A-0952 by 'Student 77', each with 4 rubric criteria, due tonight 11:59pm. Week 5 lecture recording is 74 min, with 2 slide decks. 6 TAs, each with a section; Dana is in Section B04.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
